note: Live-session recording of the SharePoint episode screens (series/tools/rec). prepare/teardown run on the laptop, not recorded. Set MG_TENANT, MG_UPN_DOMAIN and MG_PNP_CLIENT_ID in the environment before queueing (never in a file). Sign-ins are device-code, done by the owner. Episodes 1-9 chain: set MG_KEEP_CHAIN=1 while recording them in order so teardown keeps what the next episode uses; unset it for a full clean-up. The Purchase Requests list comes from episode 1 (needs episode:01 recorded with MG_KEEP_CHAIN=1).
prepare: if (-not $env:MG_TENANT -or -not $env:MG_UPN_DOMAIN -or -not $env:MG_PNP_CLIENT_ID) { throw 'Set MG_TENANT (lab tenant short name), MG_UPN_DOMAIN (sign-in domain of the lab users) and MG_PNP_CLIENT_ID (the MG Lab PnP app) in the environment first' }
if (-not (Get-PnPList -Identity 'Purchase Requests' -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue)) { throw 'Purchase Requests list not found: record episode 01 first (MG_KEEP_CHAIN=1)' }
Set-PnPListItem -List 'Purchase Requests' -Identity $i[0].Id -Values @{ RequestStatus = 'New'; DueDate = $d.AddDays(-3); Requester = $env:MG_LABADMIN_UPN } | Out-Null
Set-PnPListItem -List 'Purchase Requests' -Identity $i[1].Id -Values @{ RequestStatus = 'Approved'; DueDate = $d; Requester = $env:MG_ALEX_UPN } | Out-Null
Set-PnPListItem -List 'Purchase Requests' -Identity $i[2].Id -Values @{ RequestStatus = 'Ordered'; DueDate = $d.AddDays(4); Requester = $env:MG_ALEX_UPN } | Out-Null
Set-PnPListItem -List 'Purchase Requests' -Identity $i[3].Id -Values @{ RequestStatus = 'Closed'; DueDate = $d.AddDays(-60); Requester = $env:MG_ALEX_UPN } | Out-Null
Set-PnPListItem -List 'Purchase Requests' -Identity $i[4].Id -Values @{ RequestStatus = 'New'; DueDate = $null; Requester = $env:MG_LABADMIN_UPN } | Out-Null

screens.name: before
steps: Switch to the view 'Open requests' with the view picker
Hold on the plain, unformatted rows: an overdue, a due-today, a closed and a no-due-date request are all visible
mask: tenant host in the address bar (pipeline/mask.js)
account avatar and display name in the top bar

screens.name: after
steps: (Optional terminal inset, run before this screen: ./src/Set-ListFormatting.ps1 -SiteUrl $site -ClientId $app prints 'No findings.', four Column rows and one View row)
Point at the status pills, the red bold overdue date with the warning icon, the amber due-soon dates, the amount data bars, own requests in bold and the highlighted overdue rows
Point at the row due today: it must be amber, not red. If it is red, record it as is
mask: tenant host in the address bar (pipeline/mask.js)
account avatar and display name in the top bar

screens.name: format-pane
steps: In the 'Open requests' view, select the 'Due date' column header
Choose Column settings > Format this column
Select 'Advanced mode' and scroll to the color expression with 86400000
Hold on the JSON, then choose Cancel (do not save)
mask: tenant host in the address bar (pipeline/mask.js)
account avatar and display name in the top bar
any people names inside the JSON preview

screens.name: not-in-view
steps: Open the view picker > Save view as... > name it 'Due dates only', leave 'Make this a personal view'
Edit the view columns: keep only Title and Due date (remove Status)
Find the Closed request with the old due date and show how its date renders now, compared with 'Open requests'
Record what actually happens, then delete the personal view afterwards
mask: tenant host in the address bar (pipeline/mask.js)
account avatar and display name in the top bar

teardown: if (-not $env:MG_TENANT -or -not $env:MG_UPN_DOMAIN -or -not $env:MG_PNP_CLIENT_ID) { throw 'Set MG_TENANT (lab tenant short name), MG_UPN_DOMAIN (sign-in domain of the lab users) and MG_PNP_CLIENT_ID (the MG Lab PnP app) in the environment first' }
